RESEARCH WAS NOT TRUNCATED. The research phase ran 06:01-06:32 ET of a ~60 minute budget and closed with a RESEARCH COMPLETE block; 16 unique symbols were captured across 29 rows of candidates.jsonl, and every figure below was recomputed from source during synthesis rather than carried over on trust.

WHAT THIS REPORT IS TODAY, IN THREE GROUPS THE RANKING DOES NOT SEPARATE. Only FIVE of the sixteen rows are new money, and all five are wait:true - BMY (2), TFC (6), ALL (15) long-term, VVV (7) and DLB (3) swings. NINE are instructions on money already at risk, being every open position that still had something to decide: BCC (1) close at the open, AAL (5) close the short at the open, HII (13) set a stop at 289.00 where there has been none for 29 days, OXY (10) / UNP (12) / ONON (11) stops WIDENED to exactly 2.00 ATR, PYPL (8) a forced half-trim because no compliant stop exists in either direction, ACM (4) trim half before the close on 2026-11-16 ahead of its print, and SMMT (9) do nothing deliberately - that last row exists only to answer the 6.67% single-day fall on 2026-11-11 that a holder will see this morning and react to, which is 0.94 of one ordinary day for an instrument whose ATR is 7.57% of price, and came on the lowest volume of the last five sessions. TWO are pending unfilled orders being managed rather than positions: TLT (14) leave the 80.30 limit alone and do not chase it toward the 80.92 market, CVS (16) cancel outright. Five further open positions were checked and deliberately emit no row at all - KHC, ABT, RTX, XLU and PFE are holds with nothing changed, and re-pitching an unchanged idea is what inflated this report's own by-conviction table. The ranking rule is conviction-then-reward-to-risk, so these three groups are interleaved rather than grouped: read every catalyst.action before acting on anything, because a rank-1 row saying 'sell this at the open' sits directly above a rank-2 row saying 'do not buy this yet'.

RANKING TIEBREAK, STATED BECAUSE IT IS NOT DERIVABLE FROM THE NUMBERS. BCC and AAL are exit instructions whose reward-to-risk is undefined - a short being closed above its entry cannot produce a passing ratio, and BCC's 110 target is explicitly abandoned - so both are published with risk_reward null. Within their conviction band they are ranked FIRST, using catalyst proximity as the tiebreaker the skill allows: an unconditional at-the-open instruction is the nearest possible catalyst, where every other row is a limit that may never fill. Do not read a null ratio on those two rows, or a failing one, as a defective idea - it is the arithmetic working. CVS is treated differently on purpose: its ratio IS computable at 2.07:1 against a 2.5 long-term floor, and that failure is itself one of the two stated reasons to cancel, so it is published rather than nulled, and it ranks last in its band for exactly that reason.

RATIOS JUST ABOVE THE FLOOR - THE SIGNATURE, AND WHY IT IS NOT FITTING THIS TIME. All three long-term ideas land at 2.51 (ALL), 2.58 (BMY) and 2.62 (TFC) against a 2.5 floor, and four swings land at 2.00-2.08. That clustering is the exact pattern CLAUDE.md warns about, so it is flagged rather than glossed. In every case here the floor was cleared by moving the ENTRY down to where the trade qualifies, not by moving the target up: BMY, TFC and ALL are all wait:true with entries 10-12% below the market precisely because at the market they ratio 1.01:1, 1.00:1 and 1.03:1 - coin flips - and the published entry is the price at which the floor is actually met. The targets are each anchored to a defended multiple of fetched trailing EPS (BMY 12.8x, TFC 12.5x, ALL 10x on a 25%-haircut normalised figure). Three of the four tight swings (OXY 2.08, UNP 2.02, ONON 2.05) got there by WIDENING their stops from 1.66/1.65/1.71 ATR to exactly 2.00 ATR, which lowered their ratios from 2.50/2.45/2.40 - the opposite of the stop-walking abuse. ACM at exactly 2.00 is the one row where the ratio sits on the floor with no such explanation, and the red team should treat it as the weakest of the four 5s.

STOP AUDIT - THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL FINDING OF THE RUN. Every open position's stop was recomputed in ATRs from fetched history and four of ten were inside the floor. Three were widened (above). PYPL cannot be repaired at all: a 2.0 ATR stop at 53.00 drops it to 1.77:1 under the floor, and a profit-protecting stop clearing 2.0 ATR from the 56.50 entry would have to sit at or above 60.00, which is above the 59.48 market. With no compliant stop available in either direction, size is the only lever - hence the half-trim and the 1% sizing, and the 1.37 ATR stop stays on the row as a known, unfixable defect rather than being hidden. ABT at 2.04 ATR is compliant by 0.04 and was left alone. Independent synthesis-side recomputation confirmed all eleven swing stops and all five long-term ratios to the second decimal.

DATA SOURCES THAT FAILED. (1) Yahoo chart API 429 on both hosts, so there is no index, VIX, DXY, gold or WTI level in market_context - the volatility regime is unmeasured today. (2) Yahoo options 401 Unauthorized, so market_data.py implied failed for every symbol and NO candidate could be checked against the move the options market already prices - a real gap on DLB, VVV and ACM, all of which are pullback entries into dated earnings. (3) market_data.py short returned nulls, so there is no short-interest or days-to-cover read on anything. (4) Bitcoin history failed on all four providers, so no BTC ATR exists today and the 2.5 ATR futures stop floor could not be checked - which is why the pending /MBTZ6 short was left unamended at its published levels rather than re-pitched a third time on unverifiable numbers, and why there is no new crypto or index-futures idea. So there is no event-contract idea today, and that is a coverage gap, not a view that they were unattractive - it is also the cleanest vehicle the macro read above could not be expressed in. Insider checks DID work and were run on every equity finalist.

WHY THE COUNT AND MIX ARE WHAT THEY ARE. Zero intraday: yesterday was a +1.32% bounce inside a -2.34% month, so there was no gap to fade, and there is no 8:30 print today. No mix was manufactured in either direction. The new-idea screens were unusually unproductive and the reason is itself the finding - the 11-17/18/19 earnings slate was screened name by name (TGT, LOW, DIS, PANW, CPRT, TJX, HD, ATKR) and every one failed: the names whose fundamentals improved had already travelled, so there was no reward-to-risk left. TGT was the best fundamental setup on the board and still failed at 0.69:1, because clearing 2.0 would have needed a 186 target above anything it has traded in 200 days - it was dropped rather than dressed up. LOW's 2:1 target landed exactly on the floor after a +25% month into a binary. Nine de-rated large caps were screened for the long-term lane and one cleared (BMY); insider buying was 0 buys / 0 distinct buyers on all nine, so that confirmation is carried as evidence for none of them. ELV was rejected on the correlation cap rather than on the business, the book already holding PFE, ABT, XLV (pending) and now BMY in healthcare. MRK, GILD, TME and PAGS were rejected as UNMEASURABLE rather than unattractive - charge-distorted or non-USD fetched actuals from which no honest multiple could be built. VTRS (8.2x, four beats, improving) and KLIC are carried as live leads that only lack a pullback.

WEAKNESSES THE RESEARCH PHASE FLAGGED AGAINST ITSELF, CARRIED THROUGH RATHER THAN SMOOTHED. (a) ALL's 6.0x is built on trailing EPS of 43.71 that is almost certainly catastrophe-light peak earnings; the 25% normalisation haircut behind the 328 target is a judgement and NOT a figure traced to a filing, because the 10-Q was not read. If normalised EPS is really ~25 then 10x is 250 and there is no idea. Conviction is deliberately held at 3 and positioning is deliberately excluded from its evidence, because the fetched recommendation trend cuts against it - sell plus strong_sell rose from 1 to 3 since August even as the buy count rose, so the sell side is polarising rather than capitulating. (b) TLT is a 3 by evidence count on an idea whose macro premise the research phase explicitly described as weakened by its own fetched data; it is published as do-not-chase, wait:true, at 1% - if any score should come down on judgement it is this one. (c) DLB's two most recent surprises are its two smallest (+1.2, +1.8 against +19.7 and +40.0 earlier), so the beat margin is compressing as the sell side warms up. (d) TFC's insider signal is 2 buys by only 1 distinct buyer - one person, not a cluster. (e) Applying the evidence-count rule mechanically produces four conviction 5s (BCC, BMY, DLB, ACM), which is a lot; the rule states what the evidence supports, not that the ideas are equally good, and BMY is the strongest of them.

ARITHMETIC SELF-AUDIT. The research phase recomputed all 13 then-captured candidates and found five errors in its own work, all corrected before capture: TFC's stated current ratio (1.49 -> the true 1.00), CVS's bear case (77.33, the fetched range low sitting 1.67 under the entry and producing an absurd 17.4:1 -> 65.00, giving the failing 2.07 published here), HII's win_probability (0.52, a claimed +26-point edge -> 0.49, the actual driftless probability from the live price, asserting no edge at all), and ten of thirteen conviction scores that UNDERSTATED what their own evidence lists supported. Separately, a timestamp correction in the notes is worth knowing: the first block of headings originally carried per-entry times estimated from the model's sense of pace rather than read from the clock, wrong by up to 40 minutes, and were corrected to the verified 06:01-06:13 window.

PRICES. Every last_price is the 2026-11-11 close, fetched from finnhub at 06:25 ET and re-verified unchanged during synthesis at a session of 'pre' and an age of ~875 minutes. At 6am ET the previous close is the freshest honest equity price; it is a closed market, not stale data. No price in this report is estimated and none is null.

RED TEAM (phase 2c). FIRST, A READING NOTE: every rank number quoted in the paragraphs above is the pre-red-team rank, and two of the rows they name (TFC, ALL) are no longer recommendations at all. Ranks have been renumbered 1-14 on the unchanged conviction-then-reward-to-risk rule, so match rows by symbol rather than by number when reading those paragraphs against the list below. CUT TWO, DOWNGRADED THREE, AND FOUND ONE SYSTEMATIC ERROR RUNNING THROUGH EVERY VALUATION IDEA IN THE REPORT. The error first: all four valuation theses computed a P/E by summing four quarters of *adjusted* EPS from the earnings-surprise endpoint and then compared the result to a peer multiple quoted on a different basis. Checked against finnhub's own fundamentals for each name, the two bases agree for ALL (43.71 summed vs 44.58 epsTTM) and disagree materially for the other three, every time in the thesis's favour: BMY 6.23 vs 4.5141 (10.1x claimed, 13.61x reported), TFC 4.60 vs 4.1281 (10.9x claimed, 11.63x reported), DLB 4.11 vs 2.3558 (15.7x claimed, 26.78x reported). A multiple is only a comparison, so a mismatched basis is not a rounding difference — it invents the discount being traded. CUT TFC (rank 6): the thesis is 10.9x against USB at 11.8x, and on one consistent basis it is 11.63x against USB 11.23x trailing and 12.33x against 10.32x forward — a premium, not a discount, so there is nothing to re-rate; the 57.50 target also assumed EPS holds at 4.60 while forwardPE above trailing says consensus expects it to fall, with the latest quarter -41.82% year on year. CUT ALL (rank 15): its 6.0x is genuine, but the 328 target rested on a 25% normalisation haircut the idea itself flagged as unverified, and consensus answers it — forwardPE 8.77 implies normalised EPS near 29.9 and the latest quarter is -42.09% year on year, so 10x is about 299. At 299 against the 198 bear case the entry has to be 227 or lower to clear the 2.5:1 long-term floor; at the published 235 it is 1.73:1. It fails its own floor at any target traceable to a source. DOWNGRADED BMY 5 to 4 and cut its size from 4% to 3%: the trailing discount does not exist, though the forward one does (forwardPE 9.45), so the 80.00 target was re-derived as 12.0x forward EPS of 6.66 rather than 12.8x a summed-adjusted 6.23 — the level is unchanged and was not moved to rescue a ratio. The cheapness now rests on estimates rather than on reported earnings, which is a weaker claim and is stated as one. DOWNGRADED DLB 5 to 3: its valuation leg is not merely weaker but inverted (26.78x reported on EPS falling 13.35% year on year, not an undemanding 15.7x), so that evidence item was removed and the idea is now a revisions-and-trend trade carrying a valuation headwind, on three confirmations. DOWNGRADED ACM 5 to 3: the 77.22 target is exactly entry + 2 x risk, a ratio of 2.000:1 to three decimals, and sits above the 76.85 70-day high the thesis cites — the floor's arithmetic, not a level — and the only new fact in the row is a calendar lookup. NOT CUT, AND DELIBERATELY SO: the nine position-management rows. BCC, AAL, PYPL, SMMT, OXY, ONON, UNP, HII and ACM were attacked on their instructions rather than their ratios and the instructions hold. The three stop widenings (OXY, UNP, ONON) move risk control in the right direction — out, not in — but note all three land at exactly 2.00 ATR with ratios of 2.08, 2.02 and 2.05: both constraints are simultaneously at their binding minimum, so any uptick in ATR makes all three non-compliant at once. HII's 49% win probability is honest arithmetic, not an edge claim: 24.96/(24.96+25.80) from the live price, which the row states. TWO PIPELINE DEFECTS THE READER NEEDS, BECAUSE PHASE 2D WILL ACT ON THEM AND BE WRONG. (1) Fourteen rows were failed for a source returning 404. That source is api.nasdaq.com/api/quote/<SYM>/historical, which is the endpoint market_data.py uses for all history and which the validator itself called successfully this run to compute an ATR for all sixteen symbols — so the data is real and the probe is not. The bare URL HEADs 200 and GETs a body-level 400 for a missing assetclass parameter; with the parameter it GETs 200 and HEADs 404, so the cited form can never pass a HEAD check. All fourteen citations were repointed at the canonical Nasdaq page carrying the identical daily series (www.nasdaq.com/market-activity/stocks/<sym>/historical, verified 200 for every symbol), which is both verifiable and more use to a human reader. No figure changed. (2) Six rows were failed on bid/ask spread measured pre-market, where the quotes are indications with no depth behind them: VVV 28.35/40.00 on a stock at 35.90 is a 34% 'spread' on a name trading $96M a day, and ACM's ask of 72.00, HII's 325.00 and ALL's 269.00 are all round-number stubs. Every one of these is a limit order for the regular session and none of them executes pre-market, so the check is measuring a session the trade does not happen in. Those failures are artifacts; the surviving rows' theses are not affected. WHAT TO EXPECT FROM PHASE 2D: AAL, PYPL, HII and ACM will be demoted on checks that are real but are measuring the wrong thing, because the schema has no way to express an instruction about a position that already exists. AAL fails direction, ratio and expectancy because it is a short being CLOSED AT A LOSS at the open — its 'target' of 14.10 is the exit price, not an objective, and the row says so. HII fails 'downside is not below entry' because its new 289.00 stop is 27.00 ABOVE the 262.00 fill, which is the whole point: it locks a 19.8% gain on a position that has had no stop for 29 days. PYPL fails a 1.37 ATR stop that the row openly concedes cannot be fixed, which is why it halves the position instead. If those four reach the watchlist, read the action line, not the demotion reason: **AAL buy to close at the open, HII set the 289.00 stop, PYPL trim half at the open, ACM trim half before the 2026-11-16 close.** Note also that positions_from_report only reads `recommendations`, so a demoted row never reaches the position tracker — the OXY, UNP and ONON stop widenings are recorded only while those rows stay in the report, and a demoted HII leaves the tracker still holding no stop. The red team did not change validate_report.py: that is a logic change needing a test, not a 6am edit. Fourteen ideas survive, of which four are new money and all four are wait. Validation demoted 9 idea(s) whose numbers did not check out. 5 more carry warnings — see the validation block on each.

The macro leg got worse at the same time rather than better: the 10-year is 4.88% and rising from 4.86%, and the 2-year 4.56% from 4.51%, so the mortgage-rate relief the thesis was waiting for is being priced out, not in. recommendations.thesis: The claim is a multiple, not a catalyst — but the multiple has been rebuilt by the red team, because the published version was not computed on a basis comparable to the peers it cited. The original summed four quarterly adjusted actuals — 1.35 (Sep-26), 2.04 (Jun-26), 1.58 (Mar-26) and 1.26 (Dec-25) — to 6.23 of trailing EPS and called that 10.1x at 62.91, against large-cap pharma at 12-16x. Those are different measures: finnhub reports BMY epsTTM 4.5141 and **peTTM 13.61**, which is inside the peer range rather than at a discount to it, so the trailing-multiple discount the idea was sold on does not exist. **What does survive is the forward multiple, and it is the stronger argument anyway:** forwardPE 9.45 at 62.91 implies forward EPS of 6.66, so a re-rating to 12.0x forward is 79.9 — which is where the unchanged 80.00 target now comes from, derived rather than retained. The earnings record still says the business is not behaving like a terminal patent-cliff story: surprises of +11.9%, +10.4%, +27.2% and +17.0% across those four quarters, and the sell side has not caught up, with 19 of 34 analysts still at hold against 6 strong buy and 8 buy — a 41.2% bullish share that is nonetheless improving. **The actionable instruction today is still to wait:** at 62.91 the reward-to-risk against the stated bear case is 1.01:1, far below the 2.5:1 long-term floor, and the idea only becomes publishable as a buy inside 53-57.
recommendations.key_risk: The invalidation is concrete and is not a price: **two consecutive quarters of declining year-on-year revenue in the growth portfolio alongside a trailing EPS print below 5.00**, which would mean the cliff is outrunning the pipeline. Until that happens a falling price is an opportunity, not evidence. Two things are missing and both are why this is conviction 4 rather than 5. First, fetched insider data shows **zero open-market buys and zero distinct buyers**, so the one signal that best separates a cheap de-rating from a broken one is absent, which is why the entry sits at a 12% discount rather than at the market. Second, the cheapness now rests on **consensus forward estimates rather than on reported earnings** — on reported trailing earnings BMY is at 13.6x and there is no discount at all — so an estimate cut does not merely lower the target, it removes the thesis. There is also no dated catalyst to force the re-rating, so this can stay cheap indefinitely.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is that every patent-cliff pharma looks cheap on trailing earnings precisely because those earnings are about to fall, so 10.1x on 6.23 is a multiple of a number that will not repeat, and the 19 holds are analysts modelling the cliff rather than missing it. That is answered by the direction of the surprises rather than dismissed: the four beats run +11.9, +10.4, +27.2, +17.0 and the largest two are the most recent two, so the estimates being beaten are themselves already cliff-adjusted — the sell side is modelling the decline and the company is still coming in above it. Price is also above the fetched SMA200 of 60.26, so the tape is not confirming the terminal case. Separately, this report cancels a stale CVS limit 11.8% below market elsewhere today while setting a BMY level 11.8% below market, and the difference is deliberate: this one carries a stated bear-case price, an explicit invalidation condition and wait:true, where the CVS order carried no stop and no invalidation and had been inherited across three publications.
